 Some more stats from Como's 9-1 win at Lens if you'd indulge us.
 Como have equalled the
 most goals scored by any club in their first four major European matches
 (19), matching Queens Park Rangers in 1976. They have surpassed the Champions League record by five goals, previously held by Juventus (14 in
 1995-96).
 Lens have suffered the
 joint-heaviest defeat by a French club in major European competition,
 alongside Strasbourg’s 10-2 loss at MTK Budapest in 1961. No French side
 had previously lost a major European home match by more than five goals.
 Como are only the second
 club to score nine goals in a UEFA Champions League match, after Bayern
 München vs Dinamo Zagreb in September 2024 (9-2). They are the first
 Italian side to score nine in major European competition since Roma beat
 Altay SK 10-1 in 1962.
 Como are the first side
 to have 11 different players score or assist in a UEFA Champions League
 match, overtaking the previous record of 10 set by Benfica in their 6-1
 win against Maccabi Haifa in November 2022.

 'Strange goal to concede for such a brilliant goalkeeper' published at 22:34 GMT 22:34 GMT 
 FT: RB Leipzig 2-3 Man City 
 Owen Hargreaves 
Former Manchester United midfielder on TNT Sports 
 I think it was a cross [Baku goal], but obviously it nestles into the net and for all players at the top you get punished if you make mistakes. 
 You have to hope for the best and plan for the worst and [Gianluigi Donnarumma] doesn't really need to be there, and be that far off his line because if he's a yard back he just picks the ball up quite easily. 
 He probably just didn't get back in the position that he anticipated, he probably thought he was closer to the goal than he was, but strange goal to concede for such a brilliant goalkeeper.

 'A lot to learn' published at 22:31 GMT 22:31 GMT 
 FT: Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal 
 Arsenal 
 Image source, Getty Images Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, speaking to TNT Sports: "Always we need to value winning away in the Champions League. It is extremely difficult. Two very different halves. We should have had three or four goals in the first half but we didn't do it. Right at the start of the second half we were on the back foot, very sloppy and gave balls away. Then we had to suffer. A lot to learn.
 "We should have scored more in the first half and if we didn't do that we had to go and do that in the second half.
 "We made six changes but we know the quality of the players we have. Whether we were lacking something I don't know but I would have done the same thing [again].
 "I value what the team has done now, it is 11 away games we played."

 There were moments again like that goal against PSG when Manchester City were about to get momentum in the game and he threw one in. Tonight I thought he should do better at the near post [for the first RB Leipzig goal]. There was a shot in the first half that nearly goes in. We created a lot of chances and could have scored more but the second half was completely different. They stepped up a gear and made it difficult for us and we have to learn from it. Delighted with the win but a lot of things to improve going forward.
 "Maybe they started pressing a bit higher with more intensity. We had too many giveaways especially in the final third. There was too much running from box to box and we have to manage those reactions and go for the third and fourth goal.

 'We need to step up a bit' published at 22:17 GMT 22:17 GMT 
 FT: RB Leipzig 2-3 Man City 
 Manchester City 
 Manchester City striker Erling Haaland speaking to TNT Sports about being ready when chances come: "Not sure how many touches I had today, not the most but what is the most important is that I managed to help the team to win. I think we need to step up a bit, when we were 1-0 up I think we needed to go at it, go for the second goal and then the third - that's what we have to do. We have to work on that."
 What improvements? "Keeping the ball, when to keep it when to go, working together offensively and defensively. You can always be better and there's always a new chance. A new game in three days so that's lovely."
 On being ready for chances: "You can look at it that it's difficult to keep concentrated for 100 minutes or you can look at it like it's only 100 minutes you have to stay focussed to get a chance - you can look at it in a few different ways and I look at it in the second option."

 By Shamoon Hafez Football reporter Erling Haaland scored the winner to continue his formidable goalscoring record against RB Leipzig as Manchester City returned to winning ways by collecting three points in the Champions League. 
 Enzo Maresca's side have fallen to back-to-back defeats in the Premier League and edged past Brighton on penalties in the Carabao Cup, but emerged victorious in Germany in a thrilling game that ebbed and flowed.
 City were struggling to break down the obdurate Leipzig backline and it was the home side who had the better chances in the opening exchanges.
 Antonio Nusa's effort from outside the area almost squirmed in through the grasp of Gianluigi Donnarumma but landed on top of the net, while Christoph Baumgartner curled narrowly wide of the far post.
 Having had plenty of possession without threatening, City were given a gift by home defender Castello Lukeba, who conspired to get his feet in a muddle and ended up sliding Nico O'Reilly's harmless cross into his own net.
 But the visitors returned the favour at the start of the second half - Donnarumma's recent form has been questionable and the Italian left his near post far too exposed, allowing Ridle Baku to squeeze in the equaliser.
 City restored their lead on 57 minutes through Enzo Fernandez's bullet header, but the lead was short-lived as Nusa drilled home a brilliant low finish on the hour mark to draw Leipzig level again.
 Maresca's men pushed on and got their reward through captain Haaland, who slid home the winner on 78 minutes from Elliot Anderson's low cross for his 13th goal in nine games against Leipzig.
 Man City ratings 
 Gianluigi Donnarumma: The mistakes are starting to stack up for the Italian. Saved Antonio Nusa's drive from range unconvincingly and had a shocker for Ridle Baku's equaliser. 4 
 Matheus Nunes: Made an important block in front of goal to deny David Raum's thumping drive and won more possession than any other City player. 7 
 Abdukodir Khusanov: The Uzbek made more clearances than any other player on the pitch but was booked late on for a rash challenge. 6 
 Marc Guehi: Restored to the starting XI after being dropped on Saturday, the England international showed an improvement after recent shaky performances. 6 
 Nico O'Reilly: An attacking threat. Provided the cross for the opening goal and should have scored when he sent a free header wide. 7 
 Elliot Anderson: Another all-action performance from Anderson. Made more tackles than any team-mate, no player won more duels and laid on Erling Haaland's winning goal. 8 
 Enzo Fernandez: The £125m man had gone seven games without contributing a goal or assist but came up trumps with a thumping header. 7 
 Iliman Ndiaye: Making his first Champions League start, the Senegal international was deployed from the left and sent in an inch-perfect cross for Fernandez's goal. 7 
 Phil Foden: Lost possession much too often and had little influence in the final third, but he did nearly score the opener with an effort that drifted inches wide. 5 
 Rayan Cherki: Dragged a shot wide from inside the box early on but improved later in the game by clipping a shot against the crossbar. 6 
 Erling Haaland: Skipper for the night, Haaland was feeding off scraps but came alive late on to score the winner. 7
